issues.t: Whistle, squeal and rough idle from a cracked camshaft cover
issues.sym: A whistling, squealing or chirping noise from the engine, a rough or shaky idle, sometimes stalling, and a check engine light, often with code P0171 (running lean).
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve is built into the plastic-and-aluminum camshaft cover. Its rubber diaphragm cracks and lets extra air into the engine. GM gave special coverage on some 2016 and 2019 Cascadas; 2017 and 2018 owners report the same failure without coverage.
issues.next: Get it fixed soon, because a big vacuum leak can cause stalling. Ask a Buick dealer to check your VIN for special coverage N192291620 or N232395320 before paying.

issues.t: Rear window separating from the convertible top
issues.sym: The glass rear window starts lifting from the fabric top at a lower corner. The gap grows over time, and rain gets into the car.
issues.why: The adhesive bond between the rear glass and the soft top fails. GM bulletin 17-NA-216 covers this, and it is the most common complaint for every Cascada year.
issues.next: Keep the top up and avoid car washes until it is repaired. Don't drive at highway speed with a large gap, since the glass could come loose. A dealer may replace the whole top; ask about bulletin 17-NA-216 and any goodwill help.

issues.t: Loss of power from turbocharger failure
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses power or slows down while driving, with the check engine light and sometimes a transmission warning.
issues.why: Owners have reported failed turbochargers to NHTSA, including one at about 50,000 miles. A failed turbo can't build boost, so the small engine feels very weak.
issues.next: Move to a safe spot if power drops in traffic. Have the codes read and the turbo checked. Ask whether the powertrain warranty (5 years/60,000 miles) still applies.

issues.t: No crank or no start with the security light on
issues.sym: The car won't crank or start, or starts and then stalls, and the security (anti-theft) light is on.
issues.why: GM bulletins in the PIC5650 series cover a problem where the theft-deterrent system does not recognize the key or a module drops off the network.
issues.next: Try your spare key fob and replace the fob battery. If it still won't start, have it towed to a dealer that can read the security codes.

issues.t: Engine cranks by itself and then won't start
issues.sym: The starter turns the engine over unexpectedly, or keeps cranking, and then the car won't start.
issues.why: GM issued preliminary information (PIP5569A) to help dealers track down this starting fault.
issues.next: Have it towed to a Buick dealer and ask them to check bulletin PIP5569A. Note when it happens so they can match it.

issues.t: Misfire, rough running and check engine light
issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, especially at idle, and the check engine light flashes or stays on with misfire codes.
issues.why: GM bulletins (PIP5628G and PIP5029H) cover misfires from ignition, fuel injector and carbon buildup problems on these engines.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have the codes read soon.

issues.t: Steam from the grille area
issues.sym: White steam or vapor rising from the front grille or radiator area, often on cool or damp days.
issues.why: GM bulletin 19NA104 covers vapor from the grille area. It is often moisture burning off, but it can also mean a coolant leak.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and watch the temperature gauge. If the level drops, or you smell sweet coolant, have the cooling system checked.

issues.t: Water sloshing inside the rear quarter panel
issues.sym: A sound of water moving back and forth behind the rear seat when you turn or brake.
issues.why: Water from the convertible top drains collects inside the rear quarter panel and drains too slowly. GM bulletin 17-NA-149 covers the fix.
issues.next: Have the drains cleared before water causes rust or electrical problems. Mention bulletin 17-NA-149.

issues.t: Windows move up or down on their own
issues.sym: Side windows go up or down without anyone touching the switch, including a rear window that drops when the car starts.
issues.why: On the Cascada the convertible roof control module also runs the side windows, so a fault in that module or a window switch can move them unexpectedly.
issues.next: Don't leave the car with the windows down. Keep hands clear of windows. Have a dealer check the roof module and redo the window learn procedure.

issues.t: Windows close automatically with the roof (recall)
issues.sym: Windows close on their own when the top closes, or can be closed with the key fob from far away.
issues.why: Some early 2016 cars had their convertible roof control module replaced with the wrong part, so the windows could close without anyone watching. GM recall 16V844000.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Keep hands and pets clear of the windows until the dealer installs the correct module for free.

issues.t: Convertible top won't open or close
issues.sym: The top stops partway or won't move, and the dash may say "Extend cargo shade to operate top."
issues.why: The top will only move if the trunk cargo shade and pass-through flap are fully in place. GM bulletin 16NA352 covers setting them correctly; other bulletins cover top faults.
issues.next: Make sure the cargo shade divider in the trunk is pulled out and latched, then try again. If it still won't work, close the top manually per the owner's manual and see a dealer.

issues.t: Holes wearing through the soft top near the rear
issues.sym: Small holes or worn spots in the fabric top near the rear side panels.
issues.why: Parts of the top frame can rub through the fabric. GM bulletin 16NA324 covers replacing the top cover.
issues.next: Have it looked at early, before water gets in. Ask the dealer about bulletin 16NA324.

issues.t: Battery goes dead after short drives
issues.sym: The battery is flat after the car sits for a few days, especially if you mostly make short trips.
issues.why: GM bulletin SB-16-NA-126 traced battery drain on some cars to the tail lamps and called for replacing them.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested, then ask a dealer to check for parasitic drain and bulletin SB-16-NA-126.

issues.t: Low oil pressure warning
issues.sym: A low oil pressure message or check engine light, sometimes with code P0521.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIP4786C covers diagnosing low oil pressure warnings on this engine, which can come from low oil, a bad sensor or a real oil pressure problem.
issues.next: Pull over and turn off the engine. Check the oil level. If it is full and the warning stays on, don't drive it; have it towed for diagnosis.

issues.t: Power loss in very cold weather
issues.sym: On very cold days the engine loses power or runs poorly, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze inside the turbo intake system. GM bulletin PIP5540 covers inspecting for this icing.
issues.next: Let the car warm up and see if it clears. If it keeps happening, ask a dealer about bulletin PIP5540.

issues.t: Black smoke at startup after sitting
issues.sym: A puff of black smoke from the tailpipe when you start the car after it has been parked a while.
issues.why: GM issued preliminary information (PIP5189B) to dealers about black smoke at startup after the car has been parked for a while.
issues.next: If it is just a puff that clears, it is usually not urgent. If the smoke continues or the engine runs rough, have it checked.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin (PIT5099G) to diagnose A/C systems that blow warm air.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and refrigerant charge checked. Don't top it off without finding the leak.

issues.t: Radio goes blank or shows Theft Locked
issues.sym: The radio stops working, shows a blue screen, or displays "Theft Locked."
issues.why: GM bulletins (16-NA-107 and PIC6111C) cover radio software and theft-lock problems.
issues.next: Try turning the car fully off for a few minutes. If it continues, a dealer can update or unlock the radio.

issues.t: Bluetooth, voice control or OnStar not working
issues.sym: Phones won't pair or drop out, voice commands are ignored, or OnStar can't connect.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins on Bluetooth and voice recognition. OnStar on these cars also lost service when 3G networks shut down.
issues.next: Delete and re-pair your phone and update its software. Ask a dealer about radio updates and whether an OnStar hardware upgrade is available.

issues.t: Seat belt presenter arm noisy or not working
issues.sym: The arm that hands you the front seat belt grinds, makes a loud noise, or stops moving.
issues.why: Convertibles like the Cascada have a powered arm that reaches the belt forward. Owners report the motor failing, and parts can be on back order.
issues.next: You can still reach back for the belt and buckle up normally. Have the presenter motor replaced so the belt sits where you can reach it.

issues.t: Passenger shoulder belt knocks in the wind
issues.sym: With the top down, the passenger shoulder belt flaps or knocks against the trim.
issues.why: GM bulletin 16-NA-285 covers repositioning the belt so wind doesn't move it.
issues.next: Not a safety risk, but a dealer can reposition the belt per bulletin 16-NA-285.

issues.t: Side mirror glass shakes at speed
issues.sym: The view in the side mirrors shakes or flutters while driving.
issues.why: GM bulletin 16NA075 covers mirror glass shake on the power-folding mirrors.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply bulletin 16NA075.

issues.t: Red brake warning light flickers on
issues.sym: The red brake warning light comes on for a moment and goes off.
issues.why: GM bulletin PI1410B describes an on-and-off red brake light that can be normal in some conditions. Low brake fluid from worn pads or a leak is another common cause.
issues.next: Check the brake fluid level. If it is low, or the light stays on, or the pedal feels soft, don't drive until the brakes are inspected.

issues.t: Alarm goes off by itself
issues.sym: The car alarm sounds even when it hasn't been armed or nobody touched the car.
issues.why: Owners report false alarms. A door, hood or trunk switch that reads open, or a weak battery, can trigger the alarm.
issues.next: Make sure the trunk and doors are fully latched and test the battery. If it continues, a dealer can check which sensor set off the alarm.
